newsitem.title: JAPAN: Stable forex rates important for Japan economy - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Stable forex rates important for Japan economy - MOF.

text.p: The stability of foreign exchange rates is important for the Japanese economy, Japanese Vice Finance Minister Takeshi Komura told reporters on Monday.

Asked whether the recent weakening of the yen would lead to an increase in Japan's trade surplus, Komura said: "I would like to refrain from commenting on recent market movements. It is important for Japan's economy that foreign exchange rates stabilise and we will continue to watch the market and respond in an appropriate and timely manner."
Komura also said the present surplus in Japan's trade account was temporary and was due to the effects of a rise in the national consumption tax in April.
The vice minister said Japan had not received any official request from Thailand in connection with an expected rescue package for its economy.
"There has not been anything in the form of an official request," he said.

He added, however, that Japan was in close contact with Thai authorities and that it will cooperate with any rescue package if necessary, although he could not say anything at this time about the content of any Japanese measures.
He also said Japan was aware that Thailand was in talks with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), but the IMF and Thailand still had not finalised specific measures for a rescue package.
